method: Exact scaled-integer arithmetic on the decimal string (first derivation, method A; full per-item work in first-derivation.md): each input is parsed as sign + integer digits + fraction digits, never as a binary float. The unsigned value is scaled by 10^2 exactly into an integer quotient Q (integer digits followed by the first two fraction digits) and an exact decimal remainder r formed by the remaining fraction digits. Q is incremented iff r > 1/2, or r = 1/2 exactly and Q is odd (ties to the even neighbor); every '...5'-terminated input yields r = 1/2 exactly under this treatment. The rounded Q is rendered as <integer>.<two decimals>, the integer part comma-grouped every three digits, and negative inputs are wrapped in parentheses unsigned. A second, disjoint-method derivation (digit-string tie inspection) by an isolated child session and its per-item agreement record are PENDING-INTEGRATION per child/integration-plan.json; the answers above stand as final only if root integration confirms all-12 agreement.
